title: Group laws keep their top rigid
claim: Group laws keep their top rigid. A group's coset law composes like cycles exactly when every subgroup has a unique maximal normal subgroup (KNOT-CIRCUITS Theorem 1). Such a group has all Sylow subgroups cyclic, its unique maximal normal subgroup N has prime index q, and every subgroup's abelianization is a cyclic p-group. Up to order 60 these are the cyclic p-groups and 18 non-abelian groups: the dihedral groups of order 2p^k (p^k = 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 17, 19, 23, 25, 27, 29) and C5:C4, C7:C3, C13:C3, C13:C4, C11:C5, C19:C3. (1) Every knot of such a law is pulled back from a linear relation over a cyclic p-group quotient of its ranges. (2) Every system's solutions are pulled back from a linear system over the cyclic p-groups R_v/R_v' of the variables' ranges, and a global failure lives in one prime, as a square system over Z_(p^K). (3) By RIGID-SELECTION D the top image in G/N after any removal from a global failure on a substrate is at most one line: the top is rigid. (4) The law is rigid when the order is squarefree, and keeps knots below its top in C5:C4 and D9, through their cyclic subgroups of order 4 and 9. Checked: the list from all metacyclic presentations up to order 60; brute force on small substrates for the non-abelian groups up to order 24 (saturation and top); the examples in C5:C4 and D9 by brute force inside the cyclic subgroups.
failure_conditions: A group up to order 60 whose subgroups all have a unique maximal normal subgroup but which is missing from the list, or has a non-cyclic Sylow subgroup.
A global failure of such a group law whose solutions after a removal are not saturated by the derived subgroups of the ranges, or whose top image is not rigid.
foundation_claim_scope: Coset laws of finite groups whose subgroups each have a unique maximal normal subgroup.
